newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM calls for casino ban.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM calls for casino ban.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Monday he believed dozens of casinos were operating illegally in the capital and should be closed.
"My opinion is that the government must shut all casinos," Ranariddh told reporters after attending a health seminar, adding that he believed all casinos in the kingdom were illegal.
He said if Cabmodia wanted to allow casinos to operate, the National Assembly should adopt a casino law.

The prince was responding to media reports that a Malaysian company, Ariston Sdn Bhd, had complained that the government had reneged on an agreement to give it the sole right to operate casinos under the terms of a $1.3-billion-development project.

The Cambodia Daily on Monday quoted Ariston executive K.C. Chan as saying the government had broken their agreement by not closing about 40 casinos that have opened in the capital since a half-hearted crackdown in late 1995.
Ariston runs a floating casino and says it was given the exclusive right in 1995 to operate casinos here for 10 years.
The government in late 1995 closed all casinos in Phnom Penh except the Ariston operation and one in a local hotel. Most have since reopened, and many new casinos have opened with impunity.
